title: v1: email work order to selected shop (mailto)
description:
Builds on the shop finder's 'Use this shop' selection. Add an 'Email this work order' button on the work-order view when a shop is selected: opens a mailto: link with subject ('Service request — <bike type>, <miles> miles') and a plain-text body listing the overdue/due-soon items with wear evidence, rider mileage summary, and a 'generated by Bike Health Report' footer.
Caveats to handle: OSM rarely has shop email addresses (email/contact:email tags are sparse) — when absent, leave the To: field empty so the rider fills it in, or show the shop's phone/website as the fallback contact path. mailto body length limits (~2000 chars safe) — keep the body terse. URL-encode newlines properly.
Stepping stone toward the v2 shop-side view (spec press release roadmap item c: shops receive work orders and pre-order parts).
Verification: vitest for the mailto URL builder (encoding, length cap, empty-email case); manual click-through confirms the OS mail compose opens prefilled.

title: v1: service log — mark work done, reset component wear for future reports
description:
After the work order (or on any card), let the rider mark a component as replaced/serviced (date defaults to today, mileage auto-filled from ride data). Store the service log client-side in localStorage — keeps the no-accounts promise; key by Strava athlete/gear id when available so it survives across sessions on the same browser. On the next report, entries flow in as baselines so serviced components show fresh.
Engine prerequisite: generalize the baseline mechanism — Baselines is currently hardcoded to chain/tires and only works for mileage components (the post-M2 altitude review flagged both limits: string-keyed lookup and the unreachable else-branch for time-unit components). Replace with per-component {key: {date|miles_ago}} accepted for ANY component incl. time-based (bar tape, sealant, safety check dates).
UX sketch: checkbox per work-order line 'done on <date>' -> saved; report cards get a small 'I replaced this' affordance. Show 'last serviced' on cards when known.
Related: bikewrench-5rh, bikewrench-our (conservative-default assumptions this softens).
Verification: engine tests for generalized baselines incl. months-unit; vitest for the log store; e2e: mark chain done -> rerun report -> chain green at 0 miles.

title: v1: local bike shop finder — location, nearby shops, hours & contact info
description:
From the spec's one-liner ('directs you to local bike shops') — never scheduled into a v0 milestone. Cutline note: v0 excluded shop inventory/booking integration; plain discovery was not cut.
Build: browser Geolocation API (with graceful text-input fallback for denied permission / no GPS), then query a places source for nearby bike shops; render name, distance, address, phone, website, today's hours. Natural home: alongside the Shop Work Order ('shops near you that can do this work'), and include the chosen shop's name/address on the printed work order.
Data-source decision (needs a spike): Google Places has the best hours/contact data but needs an API key billed per request — key must live server-side, so add a FastAPI proxy endpoint (first real reason the backend exists beyond the wear engine). OpenStreetMap/Overpass is free and keyless but hours/phone coverage is patchy. Privacy: keep the no-persistence promise — coordinates go to the places API only, never stored.
Verification: mock places responses in vitest; drive permission-granted and permission-denied flows; confirm work order prints with a selected shop.
close_reason: Shipped: OSM/Overpass shop finder on the work order; verified with real Boulder data

title: v1: per-bike reports via Activity Gear picker
description:
Multiple bikes is a v0 cutline; this is the v1 follow-up. The plumbing is half-done: parseActivities.ts already reads the Activity Gear column and every RideSummary carries gear. Build: after parsing, if >1 distinct non-empty gear value, show a 'Which bike?' picker (gear names + ride counts + total miles each), filter rides to the selection, run the existing report unchanged. No engine changes needed. Edge cases: rides with empty gear (offer 'unassigned' bucket or fold into a chosen bike); single-gear exports skip the picker entirely. Related: bikewrench-280 (assumption record).
Verification: vitest for the gear-grouping helper; drive the picker flow with a two-bike sample CSV.

title: Assumption: ride filter = Ride/Gravel Ride/Mountain Bike Ride/E-Bike Ride; Virtual Ride excluded; Strava distances are km
description: frontend/src/lib/parseActivities.ts RIDE_TYPES: Virtual Ride (trainer) excluded — trainer miles do wear the chain but not tires/brakes; v0 excludes them entirely. Distance column assumed km (Strava export default), converted at 0.621371. Rows with unparseable date/distance/time are silently dropped.

title: Assumption: health score = uniform-weight mean of per-component remaining life
description: engine/report.py: score = 100 * mean(clamp(1 - pct_used, 0, 1)). No component weighting (a worn chain counts the same as bar tape); overdue clamps at 0 so extra overshoot doesn't drag further. Spec doesn't define the formula.

title: Assumption: time-based wear runs from first ride in history to today
description: engine/report.py: bar tape / cables / sealant / safety check use months_between(first_ride, as_of=today), months = days/30.44. Long histories make all time-based items overdue; sealant especially (3-4mo interval).

comments.author: Holly French
comments.text: Partially addressed post-M2: optional bike_date baseline caps time-based wear at the bike's acquisition/service date (commit a0d437c). Default without bike_date is still full-history-conservative.

title: Assumption: 'not sure' and untracked components assume wear over the entire ride history
description: engine/report.py _miles_used(): chain/tires without a baseline, and ALL other mileage components (cassette, pads, BB, chainrings), use total history miles — i.e. never replaced. Conservative per spec, but a 10-year Strava history marks everything overdue. Consider capping or asking about recent service.

title: Assumption: status thresholds — due-soon at 75% of midpoint, overdue at 100%
description: engine/wear.py DUE_SOON_THRESHOLD=0.75. Spec defines green/due-soon/overdue but not the cutoffs. Midpoint of condition-adjusted range per spec; the 75% knee is our choice.

title: Assumption: mixed conditions = halfway between dry and wet multiplier
description: engine/wear.py condition_multiplier(): spec only defines a wet multiplier; 'mixed' is interpolated as (1.0 + wet_mult)/2. Not from the spec.

title: Assumption: road = rim pads, gravel/MTB = disc pads
description: engine/wear.py WEAR_TABLE: no brake-type question in the 3-question flow, so brake pad intervals are picked by bike type (road->rim 1500-3000mi, gravel/MTB->disc 3000-6000mi). Wrong for disc road bikes (increasingly common) and rim MTB/gravel. Revisit: add a 4th question or a toggle.
